build.//: EXPO_PUBLIC_* values live here rather than in .env because .env is gitignored, and a build triggered from GitHub clones the repo without it. The app treats missing Supabase config as 'run on-device only', so a cloud build would have installed, opened, and quietly had no backend — which looks like success. These belong in the repo for the same reason they are safe in it: they are compiled into the APK regardless, and access is decided by Row Level Security, not by hiding them. The service role key is a different thing entirely and never appears here.

development.//: Build this first. It produces a dev client — the app shell with your native modules compiled in — which is what makes push, deep links and haptics testable at all. Expo Go cannot do those.

preview.//: A release build you can hand to someone. APK rather than AAB so it installs by sideload without going through Play.

production.//: Store submission. Android emits an AAB, which is what Play requires.
